questions.prompt: Which learning setting uses labelled examples?
questions.explanation: Supervised learning learns a mapping from inputs to known labels.

options: Good training performance but poor performance on unseen data
A model that is too simple
questions.explanation: An overfit model memorises noise in the training data.

questions.prompt: On a dataset where 99% of examples are negative, which pair of metrics is more informative than accuracy?
options: Bias and variance of the weights
questions.explanation: Accuracy can be 99% for a model that predicts only the majority class; precision and recall expose that.

questions.prompt: What does L2 regularisation add to the loss?
options: A penalty on the sum of absolute weights
A penalty on the sum of squared weights
A penalty on the number of layers
questions.explanation: L2 (ridge / weight decay) penalises squared weights; L1 penalises absolute weights.
